parts.description: Overview of the lessons being taught in this course.

parts.title: 1 | Cirrus Skybox [10:06]
parts.description: Create a Cirrus Skybox with the new Skybox utility. Cirrus clouds often feature channels of wispy noise that define the look of the cloudscape. Learn how to export the skybox as a VDB file for use in many other kinds of software, such as Unreal.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2 | Cumulus Skybox [9:08]
parts.description: Explore techniques for creating a Cumulus Skybox with the Skybox node. This look features distinct forms of billowing towers of clouds with strandy wisps interconnecting them. Learn how to export the skybox as a VDB file.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 3 | Nimbostratus Skybox [10:58]
parts.description: Learn how to create a Nimbostratus Skybox with the Skybox tool. This creates an ambient thick sky layer with artistic gaps for sun shafts and breaks in the noise. Learn how to export the skybox as a VDB file.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 4 | Cloud Tools [11:30]
parts.description: Discover a wide range of new utilities to generate and form your own clouds with extreme customizability and detail. parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 5 | Render Targets 2 Volumetric Cloud [8:54]
parts.description: Learn about the early days of the clouds behind the Project Pegasus environment. This video will give you a first step into understanding how to draw 3D render targets to the Volumetric Cloud system in Unreal Engine.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 6 | Sparse Volume Textures [5:44]
parts.description: Witness the system which was utilised for the clouds in the Project Pegasus environment. Learn the advantages of real-time cloudscaping and ease of use controls such as quick density changing and translation of clouds at the last minute of production.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-10 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 7 | Optimization [3:52]
parts.description: Take a first step into learning some of the optimization techniques for clouds used throughout development of Project Pegasus. Discover some important parameters that Unreal does not necessarily highlight as important.

parts.title: 1 | What is Flora? [05:46]
parts.description: George Hulm introduces the Flora tools, explains the concept behind them, and talks about why he took on the challenge of designing a new set of foliage tools. George has developed a number of foliage tools, ranging from standard modelling to simulating foliage growth. With Flora, he imagined tools that sat somewhere between the two solutions with the control of modelling tools and the natural results of simulation.

parts.title: 2 | A Technical Introduction [06:30]
parts.description: Feike Postmes overviews the basic Flora nodes and explains how they function. Feikie took over development from Geroge, and built the Flora tools being demonstrated. Feike will show how the controls aim to mimic the rules of nature whilst also providing controls for artistic direction.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-11 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 3 | Scotts Pine Breakdown [48:14]
parts.description: Tilman Milsh gives an overview of an early example he used to test the Flora tools. Tilman uses his experience with other foliage tools to inform and direct the development of Flora. Because tool development doesn't have a straightforward path, Tilman provides insight into how he used these prototype tools.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-11 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 4 | In-depth Look at Flora [1:05:03]
parts.description: Tilman takes a deeper look at the Flora tools and demonstrates how the tools function and build complex and natural plant structures. He then compares this approach to how other foliage tools function.

parts.title: 2.1 | A Quick Introduction To VEX [7:22]
parts.description: Those new to VEX should know some basic principles, such as what a variable is and how to structure a “for loop.” This short video will introduce some of those basic VEX principles.

parts.title: 2.2 | Color Layer Setup [10:13]
parts.description: In this lesson, you’ll begin setting up the nodes for the “Color Layer” digital asset. This digital asset will allow you to use the previously created masks to add color to the heightfield layers. In this first section set up the required nodes and parameters.

parts.title: 2.3 | Color Layer - Writing VEX [12:21]

parts.title: 2.5 | Color Layer - Color Tips [10:57]
parts.description: Using the new Color Layer Digital Asset, you can begin building a color map for your landscape. In this lesson learn some tips to help you pick accurate colors in Houdini.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 3.1 | Color Adjust - Setup [8:43]
parts.description: Learn how to use a heightfield wrangle and VEX to adjust the hue, saturation, and brightness of the heightfield’s color. This can be used with a mask to adjust only selected areas of the color map to add additional details.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 3.2 | Color Adjust - Save As a Digital Asset [6:20]
parts.description: Save the nodes as a Digital Asset to create a reusable tool that can be combined with different masks to build up extra layers of details on the heightfield color.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 4.1 | Occlusion Mask - Setup [9:11]
parts.description: Over the next few lessons, you’ll learn how to create interesting masks to be used with the Color Adjust tool. The first is an occlusion mask that layers occlusion for small, medium and large features.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 4.2 | Occlusion Mask - Save As a Digital Asset [7:47]
parts.description: Save the assembled nodes as an Occlusion Mask Digital Asset.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 5.1 | Texture Mask - Setup [14:54]
parts.description: This second mask tool will create an interesting textured mask that combines noise, curvature, and slope masks.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 5.2 | Texture Mask - Save As a Digital Asset [15:39]
parts.description: Save the nodes as a Texture Mask Digital Asset.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 6.1 | Unreal - Create The Landscape Material [46:45]
parts.description: With the color map complete, the heightfield and color map can be exported from Houdini and imported into Unreal. In this video, learn how to set up an Unreal Project, how to use a HDA to import the landscape into your level, and how to begin building a landscape material.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 6.2 | Unreal - Importing The Color Map [14:40]
parts.description: In the final video, you’ll import the color map and combine it with the tiling textures to add additional detail to the landscape.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-12 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

series.material_association: Series-level download bundle only; per-lesson dependency mapping must be verified in the original project before implementation

source_archives.series_title: Project Pegasus | Roads, Tracks and Rivers

parts.title: Introduction
parts.description: An overview of the Linescaping process used in these lessons.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.1 | Paths and Costs [16:25]
parts.description: Learn the basics of the find-shortest path node in Houdini, such as costs and how to supply it with the correct inputs to create a simple path across the terrain.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.2 | Waypoints [22:10]
parts.description: Learn how multiple user-defined waypoints can be used to drive the creation of longer paths that travel through more than one destination.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.3 | Discontinuous Paths [13:16]
parts.description: Learn how multiple disconnected user defined paths can be defined and correctly resolved by the find-shortest-path node to begin building a more complicated road network.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.4 | Per Neighbour Costs [23:36]
parts.description: Learn how we can be more descriptive with costs by providing a cost array, instead of a simple cost per point, and how this can be used to produce more interesting and intricate paths.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.5 | Directional Costs [12:05]
parts.description: Learn how we can introduce directional costs, building on the previous work and further advancing the intricacy and possibilities of our pathfinding system.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.6 | Custom Costs [14:26]
parts.description: Learn how to create a setup that is flexible enough to allow custom costs to be considered, in addition to the predetermined costs that we have provided by default with the tool.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.7 | HDA [17:58]
parts.description: Learn how to convert our graph into a digital asset which can be shared and used in other packages such as Unreal.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1.8 | Iterations [29:54]
parts.description: Explore the potential and the flexibility of the tool by using it to produce a variety of different results.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.1 | Unreal Landscape Splines [20:29]
parts.description: The basics of using Houdini splines to deform an Unreal Landscape.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.2 | Intro to Scriptable Tools [18:57]
parts.description: An introduction to the Scriptable Tools Framework, Editor Utilities and the Houdini Engine Public API in blueprints in Unreal.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.3 | Debugging and Scheduling [18:58]
parts.description: Getting to grips with Blueprints and the Houdini Engine Public API.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.4 | Managing HDA and Spline State [22:45]
parts.description: Dealing with tool sessions and Unreal Landscape Spline peculiarities.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.5 | Configuring Unreal Spline Inputs [25:41]
parts.description: Configure the Pathfinder HDA to support Unreal Spline Inputs from the Unreal Scene.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.6 | Gizmos! [17:21]
parts.description: Learn how to create Gizmos in your Unreal tool which enable the user to modify created Splines.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.7 | More Gizmos! [33:06]
parts.description: Learn how to extend and insert points on existing splines in Unreal, as well as delete points.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.8 | Porting Tools and Materials [22:04]
parts.description: Bring the tools out of our whitebox environment and into the real world, using the Landscape and material created in Ian's workshop.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.9 | Promoting Parms [16:03]
parts.description: Give users the same degree of control they are used to in Houdini by promoting all the remaining HDA parms to the Property Set in Unreal.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2.10 | Advanced River Tool [25:40]
parts.description: A lightning tour of an Advanced River Tool built with Houdini, Scriptable Tools and Unreal's water system. Push HDAS beyond their intended limits in order to communicate with any system via blueprint, and ensure a  lightning fast user experience by minimizing data throughput. Viewers are challenged to take what that have learned throughout this series so far and push their understanding to the next level through independent learning.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-13 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 1 | Editor Utility Widgets vs Scriptable Tools [8:28]
parts.description: Explore the differences between the two main editor tools available in Unreal Engine: Editor Utility Widgets and Scriptable Tools. Note their advantages and disadvantages unique to each other and learn what is best suitable for your needs.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-15 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 2 | Creating HDAs in Unreal [7:06]
parts.description: Learn the basics of the Houdini Engine Public API and how to instantiate assets in an Unreal Scene, as well as how to use SinglePropertyView to setup options for where and how to instantiate.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-15 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 3 | Manipulating Inputs and Parameters of HDAs [10:16]
parts.description: Gain knowledge on how to utilise the Houdini Engine Public API to bind inputs and manipulate parameters of HDAs currently in the scene or recently instantiated.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-15 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing

parts.title: 4 | Use PDG TOPnets in Unreal [5:44]
parts.description: Assuming you have a basic knowledge of PDG TOPnets in Houdini, this video will help you translate your functions of cooking and controlling PDG networks in Unreal. As well as some useful code snippets to do with Editor Utility Widgets.
parts.material_association: Shared PEG-15 series bundle; no inferred per-lesson pairing
